items.title: Existing appointments' turnover buffer (bufferAfter / staff bookingBuffer) is not reserved → back-to-back slots offered
items.notes: ⚠ NEEDS CARE + A SEMANTICS DECISION (loop deferred): getAvailability blocks only [start,end] of existing appts; the buffered footprint applies only to the NEW slot, so turnover silently vanishes and two services book back-to-back with 0 gap. Fix = pad each existing appt's blockedRange by its service bufferBefore/bufferAfter + staff bookingBuffer. BUT how two ADJACENT appts' buffers compose (sum of prior.bufferAfter + next.bufferBefore, vs max) is a product decision, and this modifies the safety-critical double-booking engine — so it wants a supervised pass, not an unattended tick. Testable via the availability-timezone/booking-dst mock-prisma harness (assert no slot offered within bufferAfter of an existing appt).

items.title: Illegal appointment status transitions unguarded in updateAppointmentStatus + v1 PATCH + MCP cancel (complete→cancelled, revert completed, double check-in)
items.notes: ⚠ NEEDS A PRODUCT DECISION (loop flagged, didn't guess): /api/bookings/[id] uses getValidStatusTransitions where cancelled/no_show/completed have NO outgoing transitions — but the server action + v1 REST + MCP deliberately ALLOW cancelled/no_show→active (the reactivation/un-cancel feature, guarded for conflicts). The two subsystems CONTRADICT each other on whether un-cancel is legal. Applying getValidStatusTransitions uniformly would DELETE the un-cancel feature. Decision needed: is un-cancel (and un-complete) allowed? Then build the transition matrix accordingly (block completed→* and double check-in, but keep reactivation if desired). Also: extract the reactivation guard (now in 3 places) into one shared helper.
